svg.title: Timeout after acceptance: repeat identity, not the assumed side effect
svg.desc: Worker A authorizes one immutable delivery at epoch 1. The fake provider accepts it under key notification D-email as provider message P1, then its response is lost. The local row records UNKNOWN and RETRY_WAIT. At one second worker B takes epoch 2, rechecks preferences and queries the same key through a read-only lookup; expiry returns unknown rather than creating a new send. The provider returns P1 with no second acceptance. The local row becomes PROVIDER_ACCEPTED, which is not delivered or read. Epochs fence local updates; unsupported or expired lookup requires reconciliation rather than a new key.
svg.text: Controlled fake contract: read-only key lookup; history retained for 60 seconds. No real send occurs.
Key stored with immutable request bytes
Next attempt due at t=1; keep the original key.
Same provider key, target and exact bytes
Claim epoch is not a new message identity.
Lookup never creates a fresh send.
Delivery evidence and user read remain unknown until their own authenticated facts arrive.
No replay contract, expired window or another provider?
Reconcile/quarantine. A new key cannot repair uncertainty safely. Epochs do not undo remote sends.
